name: Obsidian Bluff
geological_features: Massive obsidian bluffs forming continental-scale walls
specific_features: Reflective obsidian surfaces used as improvised communication relays by passing ships
description: Obsidian Bluff is a striking rocky world where ancient volcanic activity produced continent-spanning flows of obsidian that cooled into immense glass bluffs. The bluff faces are so smooth they function as natural mirrors, reflecting the stars and the system's sun with startling clarity. Between the bluffs, plains of fractured volcanic glass crunch and glitter underfoot.

The thin atmosphere permits brilliant starfields at night, doubled by their reflection in the obsidian surfaces. During the day, sunlight bouncing between bluff faces creates dazzling light corridors and deep, perfectly black shadows. The visual effect is disorienting, as reflections and reality become difficult to distinguish from one another.

Microbial life exists in the fractures and pores of the obsidian, sustained by trace moisture and minerals leached from the glass. These organisms produce a faint darkening of the obsidian surface over time, a bioweathering pattern that planetary biologists use to map colony distribution from orbit. The colonies are ancient and remarkably widespread.

Obsidian Bluff's reflective surfaces have found an unexpected practical use: ships in the system use the bluff faces as improvised signal relays, bouncing communications off the natural mirrors. The planet has become an informal navigation waypoint, and a small settlement has grown up around the most useful reflective face, offering repairs and provisions to passing traffic.
